forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {畏怖|いふ}していませんでした

definitions.explanation: A feeling of deep respect mixed with fear in the presence of something overwhelmingly powerful, vast, or sacred. Combines reverence and a sense of one's own smallness.

examples.japanese: ⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{力|ちから}→力：01661_chikara⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{畏怖|いふ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じた→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: I felt awe at the power of nature.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古代|こだい}→古代：05324_kodai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人々|ひとびと}→人々：03141_hitobito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{畏怖|いふ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{対象|たいしょう}→対象：03393_taishou⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Ancient people regarded mountains as objects of awe.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夜空|よぞら}→夜空：09591_yozora⟧いっぱい⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{広|ひろ}がる→広がる：01980_hirogaru⟧⟦{星|ほし}→星：01510_hoshi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見上|みあ}げた→見上げる：04567_miageru⟧とき、⟦{宇宙|うちゅう}→宇宙：01861_uchuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{広大|こうだい}→広大：11328_koudai⟧さ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{畏怖|いふ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{念|ねん}→念：12766_nen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{抱|いだ}いた→抱く：02010_idaku⟧。
examples.english: When I looked up at the stars filling the night sky, I was filled with a sense of awe at the vastness of the universe.

notes:
USAGE:
{畏怖|いふ} is a literary and formal word expressing a blend of fear and reverence. It is often used in philosophical, religious, and literary contexts. The feeling is not simple fear but includes deep respect for something beyond human power.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {畏怖|いふ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{念|ねん}→念：12766_nen⟧ (a feeling of awe)
- {畏怖|いふ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧ (to feel awe)
- {畏怖|いふ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{念|ねん}→念：12766_nen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{抱|いだ}く→抱く：02010_idaku⟧ (to hold a sense of awe)
- {畏怖|いふ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{対象|たいしょう}→対象：03393_taishou⟧ (object of awe)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{畏敬|いけい}→畏敬：10033_ikei⟧: reverence, respect and awe (emphasizes the respect side more)
- ⟦{恐怖|きょうふ}→恐怖：02585_kyoufu⟧: fear, terror (pure fear without the reverence component)
- {恐|おそ}れ: fear, apprehension (general fear, can include awe in literary usage)
